slots.title: First Bouts at Medeo #5
slots.summary: Your call (Nov. 10): an encouraging 'First Bouts' piece about the club's kids starting their competitive paths at Medeo Youth Challenge #5 (Sun. Nov. 8). Seven Elite FC fencers took the step: Samuel SarroWaite, Roy Yoo, Elle Peterfreund, Nora Li, Claire Widjaja, Owen Li and Mira Shukla. For most, it was their first tournament (five confirmed firsts; Elle Peterfreund and Owen Li their second). Ian Huang was entered but has no result — we won't say he fenced. Christina Jiang withdrew and is in Club Results from NYFA the same day. No placings, no pool records, never characterize results. Clark writes it once you approve the budget. About 150 words.

slots.slot: Overheard on Reddit — Do You Need Fencing Shoes?
slots.budget: ~72w (short; Frank noted the thread is light)
slots.title: Overheard on Reddit: Do You Need Fencing Shoes?
slots.summary: Your r/Fencing thread (captured Nov. 10; posted ~Nov. 8): a beginner asked whether tennis shoes work as well as fencing shoes, at about half the price. Commenters there said indoor court shoes (squash or volleyball, e.g. ASICS Gel Rocket) do fine, and that entry fencing shoes, at about $80 to $100, wear out in a year or two. Some epee fencers prefer tennis shoes on aluminum strips. No usernames; attributed to r/Fencing commenters; labeled as opinion, not advice. Short on purpose — you flagged that the thread is light on content. Sits near First Bouts, where it's useful to new families buying gear.

slots.slot: Page 2 feature — For the Parents: What a Rating Letter Means
slots.title: For the Parents: What a Rating Letter Means
slots.summary: Reminder you asked for on Nov. 2: the rating-letters piece, now as a larger feature. A to U, what the year means (A26), how a letter is earned from event size and finish, and why a kid's letter can drop. It pairs naturally with First Bouts: every A started at U, often in a Y10 pool at a Medeo-type event. Clark writes it from the USA Fencing rules once you say go. Vet = go ahead.
